quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people or vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away.

questions.question: What is a good way to prevent fatigue on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a short break every two hours to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches you on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. On a two-lane, two-way road, if cars are backing up behind you, you must pull off and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn either right or left.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must bear either to the right or to the left.

questions.question: When you approach a flashing red traffic light, you must:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, don't panic. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the pavement by turning the steering wheel slightly. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and must always be obeyed.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians when crossing intersections or turning.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force if you crash.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs (legal and illegal), and being tired all impair your ability to drive.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped and orange with black letters. They warn you that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: A green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: When driving up a hill behind a heavy truck, you should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Limited visibility on hills makes passing illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The lower noise level of large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes only when necessary. Avoid cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle's lights or hear its siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street without an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, night driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You can see less in the dark, headlight glare can blind you, and tired or impaired drivers are more common at night.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so they can see you.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so they can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so they can see your vehicle.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When you see a child about to run into the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when you think another driver or pedestrian does not see you. For example, honk if a child runs into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: When can you legally pass another vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if you drive off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an available passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a multilane road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Roads freeze most quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded areas under trees or buildings. These spots freeze faster than other parts of the road and take longer to dry.

questions.question: Which must you obey before the other three?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: Traffic officers have authority over all signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic officers include police, fire police, highway work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What penalties can you face for giving false information on a DMV application?

options.text: A one-year suspension of your driving privileges

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: False information on a driver license or ID card application can result in a one-year suspension. It is also a class A misdemeanor, which can lead to fines and jail time.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as one train passes. Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks. Another train may be coming.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: You usually react slower to hazards.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You usually react slower to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots when changing lanes. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver should:

options.text: Slow down to check if traffic is clear.
Stop in the intersecting roadway to see 200 feet in each direction.
Stop where they can see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where they can see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point to the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery roads. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter requires extra caution. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk of a crash when using which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones and audio devices like radios and CD players are dangerous distractions that increase the risk of a crash.
